title: Whether a class can be both final and abstract
answer: No. `abstract` means the class is incomplete and is intended to be subclassed so abstract behavior can be implemented, while `final` forbids subclassing. Those requirements conflict, so Java does not allow a class to be declared both `abstract` and `final`. AeroTopo appropriately uses abstract `Product` for extension and final concrete classes such as `Orthomosaic` when further subclassing is not intended.
